subject: Post-call recap — Cobalt Systems throughput & latency alignment
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@cobaltsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Cobalt Systems throughput & latency alignment

Alex — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap while items are fresh and a short list of next actions so we stay aligned.

Call summary (30m):
- Current pain: document classification service at Cobalt is hitting p95 latency spikes during morning batch windows (up to ~750ms) and tail latencies are inconsistent after model scaling.
- Primary goal: reduce inference p95 to <= 180ms for 512-token prompts at target throughput of ~120–180 requests/sec for the peak tier, and keep p99 under 400ms.
- Model profile: you indicated moving from an internal 13B model to a larger 34B / 70B variant for higher accuracy; quantized 4-bit variants are acceptable if accuracy loss < 2% on your eval set.
- Data & constraints: request sizes vary (avg 280 tokens), KV cache reuse expected for chat-style sessions, and data residency needs US-only.

Technical notes we covered:
- Topology options: dedicated instance pool in us-west + hot fallback to hosted in us-east for surge capacity.
- Batching: target dynamic batching with 25–40ms batch windows for lower cost while preserving p95.
- Caching: prefix KV caching for repeated session context; estimated token-cache hit 15–20% based on your usage pattern.
- Quantization: suggest testing q4_0 and int8 variants; runtime supports both with performance profiles attached.

Attachments included: cobalt_slos_and_topology.xlsx (SLO/throughput matrix + two topology sketches), canonical_topology.png (diagram).

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) We’ll share a short perf-run plan and a sandbox link so you can run your prompt set against a 34B q4 variant (Priyom) — target ETA: 48 hours.
2) You to share a representative prompt set (50–100 prompts) and a small sample of traffic patterns (Ben) — target: EOD Thu.
3) Marissa to draft a recommended initial topology + batching profile for the perf run (Marissa).
4) Schedule a 1-hr deep dive with infra and your ops team to confirm failover and KMS details (Priyom/Alex).

Ask: Can you confirm the two goals above (p95 <= 180ms, throughput 120–180 rps) and whether the security team needs a separate session for SOC/compliance?

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

—
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
Attachment: cobalt_slos_and_topology.xlsx (spreadsheet), canonical_topology.png (image)

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@cobaltsys.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: solutions@cobaltsys.com, Judy Park <judy.park@cobaltsys.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 18:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Cobalt Systems throughput & latency alignment

Thanks Priyom — good recap. Confirming a few points and a couple of asks from our side: 

Confirmations:
- The p95 target of <= 180ms for 512-token requests is what we want to aim for on the peak tier. p99 budget of <= 400ms is also correct.
- We will plan to test a 34B quantized model first; accuracy bar is roughly "no more than 2% F1 degradation" vs our 13B baseline.

Questions / asks:
1) Multi-region failover: we need clarification on how warm failover would behave — is cold spin-up acceptable for >5 minute failover windows, or do you recommend a warm standby in a second region?
2) Cost: can you provide a ballpark delta between hosted burst vs dedicated reserved pool for the topology you suggested? A back-of-envelope is fine for now.
3) Security: Judy (cc'd) will own a short SOC2 questionnaire; can you send the DOC/links?

Attaching the initial security questionnaire they requested.

If you can send the perf-run plan and a sandbox link tomorrow, we’ll queue prompts and confirm a time for the deep-dive (ideally Thurs morning PT).

—
Alex Reed
Sr. Engineering Manager — ML Platforms
Cobalt Systems
Attachment: cobalt_security_questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap — Cobalt Systems throughput & latency alignment

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Alex's clarifications. Key asks: warm-standby behavior and a cost delta hosted vs dedicated. Quick internal notes below (putting together perf plan after these):

Marissa (internal): can you prioritize a short topology sketch with two flavors: 1) cost-optimized (cold-start tolerant; hosted surge) and 2) SLA-first (warm standby in us-east + reserved us-west pool)? Please include: estimated reserved GPU hours, expected p95/p99 for 34B-q4 under 120/180 rps and a recommended batching window.

Ben: please prepare a sample prompt ingestion method and a minimal anonymized traffic CSV we can share with Alex for the perf run (remove PII).

Tentative perf-run plan (high level):
- Sandbox: provisioned 34B-q4 instance (us-west) + traffic replayer with 2-minute warmup and 10-minute sustained run at 120 rps then ramp to 180 rps.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, batch sizes distribution.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 180ms at 120 rps; graceful degradation to p99 <= 500ms at 180 rps.

I’ll stitch Marissa's sketches into the XLS and send to Alex with the sandbox link.

—
Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@cobaltsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Perf-run plan & sandbox — Cobalt Systems (scheduling)

Alex — quick update and scheduling:

1) Perf-run plan attached (cobalt_slos_and_topology.xlsx) and a lightweight sandbox endpoint is ready for a dry run: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/cobalt/DEAL-1273 (credential link sent separately).
2) Proposed time for the 1-hr deep dive with infra & security: Thu 2026-08-27 09:00 PT. Does that work for you and Judy?
3) On warm failover: recommended pattern is warm standby for <5 minute RTOs (keep minimal hot pool in us-east). Cold spin-up only acceptable if RTOs can be >5min. We’ll document the exact expected warm capacity and estimated cost delta in the topology sheet (Marissa is drafting that now).
4) Cost delta: rough back-of-envelope — reserved dedicated pool (monthly commit) will be ~40–55% higher baseline than hosted-only per-token cost but gives consistent tail latency and reserved throughput; we’ll produce a detailed table tomorrow.

Next actions: we’ll send the detailed topology + cost delta by EOD Wed, you to provide the prompt set and Judy to confirm SOC2 questionnaire recipient.

Thanks — see attachments and link above.

—
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
Attachment: cobalt_slos_and_topology.xlsx (spreadsheet)
